race_context: The 'Oak Hill United School Corporation' races on the state list are for Oak Hill United School Corporation, based at 1474 N. 800 W.-27 in Converse, which runs Converse, Sweetser and Swayzee elementary schools, Oak Hill Junior High School and Oak Hill High School {in_list}{oh_home}. The state list describes the district as covering parts of Grant and Miami counties, and the board's district seats are drawn from Jackson Township in Miami County and Richland, Pleasant, Sims and Franklin townships in Grant County {in_list}{oh_board}. The October 2025 student count (ADM) was 1,478.42, and the superintendent told the board in February 2026 that the preliminary February count was about 20 students lower {oh_min_20260209}. Her fall 2026 projection on Aug. 10, 2026 was 1,437 students {oh_min_20260810}.

The superintendent is Dr. Sheri Hardman, and Chris Goris is chief financial and business officer {oh_board}{oh_min_20260608}. The board has seven members: five elected from districts and two elected at large {oh_board}. The district lists Andy Horner (District 1, Jackson Township of Miami County), Gary Green (District 2, Richland Township of Grant County), Aaron Pickering (District 3, Pleasant Township of Grant County), Justin Alberts (District 4, Sims Township of Grant County), Adam Thompson (District 5, Franklin Township of Grant County), and Scott Deaton and Scott Dubois (both At Large) {oh_board}. At the Jan. 7, 2026 reorganization meeting, the board elected Pickering president, Dubois vice president, Horner secretary and Alberts assistant secretary, each by a 6-0 vote, and reappointed Dubois as its liaison to the Indiana School Boards Association {oh_min_20260107}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: the district lists four members whose terms run from Jan. 1, 2023 to Dec. 31, 2026: Horner (District 1), Alberts (District 4), and Deaton and Dubois (At Large) {oh_board}. All four are on the ballot, so every candidate in these races is an incumbent {in_list}. Horner is the only candidate in District 1 and Alberts is the only candidate in District 4 {in_list}.

At-large seat count: the state list shows one race, 'District 6, At Large', with 'vote for 1' and both Deaton and Dubois as candidates {in_list}. The district's board page lists two at-large members whose terms both end Dec. 31, 2026 {oh_board}. If the ballot elects only one at-large member, the two incumbents are running against each other for one seat; if it elects two, both are effectively unopposed. This guide could not confirm the correct number of at-large seats from the Grant or Miami County election offices, and readers should check their own ballot.

Operating referendum (on the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot): on May 11, 2026, Barry Gardner of Policy Analytics presented a property-tax analysis to the board covering the effect of SEA 1 on assessed value, the district's revenues and spending, and operating-referendum considerations; the board then voted 7-0 to let administration keep investigating a referendum levy and communicate with the Grant and Miami county auditors and the state {oh_min_20260511}. The Chronicle-Tribune reported that the board approved the ballot question at a June 22 special meeting, making Oak Hill the second Grant County district to seek an operating referendum after SEA 1 {ct_oh_ref_jun2026}. The question asks voters to allow higher property taxes for up to eight years for purposes including keeping school resource officers and nurses, retaining teachers and staff, maintaining class sizes and student transportation, and academic and support programs, at a rate of no more than $0.3332 per $100 of assessed value and no more than $1,627,112 a year {ct_oh_ref_jun2026}. The Department of Local Government Finance approved the language on June 30, 2026, finding a median household assessed value of $150,000 and an increase of $198 a year for that home {dlgf_oh_det}. The Oct. 12, 2026 board agenda lists an operating referendum public meeting on Tuesday, Oct. 13, 2026 at the high school {oh_agenda_20261012}. Minutes of the June 22 meeting were not in the district's posted minutes folder when this guide checked {oh_minutes_folder}.

HVAC and facilities borrowing (2025-2026): the board held preliminary determination hearings on a facilities project in September and October 2025, with presentations from Gibraltar Design and Baker Tilly, and no public comment was recorded {oh_min_20250908}{oh_min_20251013}. In March 2026 it held two more hearings tied to 'recent legislative changes regarding assessed value' and approved the project and preliminary determination resolutions 7-0 on March 16 {oh_min_20260309}{oh_min_20260316}. On April 13, 2026 it approved a lease amendment and resolutions determining need and approving issuance of bonds, each 6-0 {oh_min_20260413}. On June 8, 2026 the superintendent described a $10 million 'Unified Project' approved in April, of which no more than $1,220,000 in general obligation bonds would go to renovations and improvements including site, roofing, paving and HVAC, plus buses, equipment and technology; the board approved the appropriation and final bond resolutions 7-0 {oh_min_20260608}. The superintendent reported on June 8 that the HVAC project's estimated total cost was about $17 million, and on July 13 that the original budget was about $25 million, with construction expected to start around March 8, 2027 and finish in spring 2028 {oh_min_20260608}{oh_min_20260713}. A taxable GO bond closed Aug. 6, 2026, and the Sept. 14, 2026 agenda listed approval of HVAC project bids {oh_min_20260810}{oh_agenda_20260914}.

Staffing: the June 8, 2026 board minutes list contract cancellations by reduction in force for seven positions: a high school math teacher, a sixth-grade ELA teacher, a third-grade teacher, a junior high custodian and three Converse instructional assistants {oh_min_20260608}. In September 2025 the superintendent's update on teacher bargaining listed staffing reductions, ADM, the budget estimate and health premium increases among the topics {oh_min_20250908}.

Sweetser wastewater project: in September 2025 the board voted 6-1 to approve a letter of intent to participate in regionalization of the Town of Sweetser wastewater project; the minutes do not name the member who voted no {oh_min_20250908}. Town and project representatives presented to the board in December 2025, and in February 2026 the superintendent said the district's financial team would review the legal questions and the district's debt capacity for the options presented {oh_min_20251208}{oh_min_20260209}.

Other 2025-2026 items: on April 13, 2026 the superintendent reported that the audits covering July 2023 to June 2025 were complete and that the corporation audit found a need for more separation of duties, and that corrective action plans were in place {oh_min_20260413}. On June 8, 2026 principals reported a 67% IREAD pass rate for Converse second graders and 88% for Sweetser third graders {oh_min_20260608}. In August 2026 the superintendent said she had applied for a 2027 state school safety grant to support the school resource officer provided by the Grant County Sheriff's Department, and principals described a new no-cell-phone policy {oh_min_20260810}. The 2027 budget hearing was set for Sept. 14 and adoption for Oct. 12, 2026 {oh_agenda_20260914}{oh_agenda_20261012}.

Forums and differences: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum, questionnaire or news coverage of the Oak Hill board races. All four candidates are sitting board members, and the board minutes reviewed for July 2025 through August 2026 record no split votes on the referendum resolution, the bond and HVAC resolutions or the 2026 officer elections; every recorded vote on those items was unanimous among members present {oh_min_20260107}{oh_min_20260316}{oh_min_20260413}{oh_min_20260511}{oh_min_20260608}.
